events.title: Erispoe's Bretons defeat Charles the Bald at Jengland
events.description: Near Grand-Fougeray on the border of Brittany, the Breton army of Erispoe defeated the West Frankish king Charles the Bald. By the Treaty of Angers that followed, Charles recognised Erispoe as ruler of the Bretons, with Rennes and Nantes.

events.title: English forces defeat David I of Scotland at the Battle of the Standard
events.description: Northern English levies rallied round a cart bearing a ship's mast and sacred banners near Northallerton and routed King David I's army. It was a key battle of the civil war period known as the Anarchy.
events.html: Northern English levies rallied round a cart bearing a ship's mast and sacred banners near Northallerton and routed King David I's army. It was a key battle of the civil war period known as the Anarchy.

events.title: Baldwin III takes Ascalon from Fatimid Egypt
events.description: After a siege begun in January, the Fatimid fortress of Ascalon surrendered to an army of crusaders, Templars and Hospitallers under King Baldwin III of Jerusalem. It had been the last coastal city in Palestine outside crusader control.

events.title: Henry Tudor defeats and kills Richard III at Bosworth
events.description: Richard III was killed fighting at Bosworth Field when Lord Stanley's forces turned against him. Henry Tudor took the crown as Henry VII, founding the Tudor dynasty.
events.html: Richard III was killed fighting at Bosworth Field when Lord Stanley's forces turned against him. Henry Tudor took the crown as Henry VII, founding the Tudor dynasty.

events.title: Charles I raises the royal standard at Nottingham
events.description: After negotiations proved futile, King Charles I raised the royal standard in Nottingham, beginning the First English Civil War. His forces controlled roughly the Midlands, Wales, the West Country and the north; Parliament held London, the south-east and the navy.

events.title: Benedict Arnold's ruse ends the siege of Fort Stanwix
events.description: Benedict Arnold, then fighting for the Continental Army, convinced the British by a ruse that a much larger force was arriving, and Brigadier General Barry St Leger abandoned the siege of Fort Stanwix in the Mohawk River Valley.
events.html: Benedict Arnold, then fighting for the Continental Army, convinced the British by a ruse that a much larger force was arriving, and Brigadier General Barry St Leger abandoned the siege of Fort Stanwix in the Mohawk River Valley.

events.title: The first Geneva Convention is signed
events.description: Twelve states signed the Geneva Convention protecting wounded soldiers and the medical staff caring for them. It grew out of Henry Dunant's campaign and founded modern humanitarian law.
events.html: Twelve states signed the Geneva Convention protecting wounded soldiers and the medical staff caring for them. It grew out of Henry Dunant's campaign and founded modern humanitarian law.

events.title: The Cadillac Automobile Company is founded in Detroit
events.description: Investors reorganised Henry Ford's former company as Cadillac, named after the founder of Detroit. Engineer Henry Leland's precision manufacturing made it a byword for quality.
events.html: Investors reorganised Henry Ford's former company as Cadillac, named after the founder of Detroit. Engineer Henry Leland's precision manufacturing made it a byword for quality.

events.title: Joseph Walker flies the X-15 to the edge of space
events.description: NASA pilot Joseph Walker took the X-15 rocket plane to 107.8 km, beyond the 100 km boundary of space. The record for a winged aircraft stood until SpaceShipOne in 2004.
